items.before_system: Check that your machine meets the Linux requirements.
items.install_desc: Run this command, and answer its one question: whether the VPN service starts at boot. It picks the right build for your processor.
items.install_after: It installs the VPN service and the [cmd] command. On a machine with a desktop, it also adds [app] to the application menu.
items.commands_desc: They work from any administrator's terminal, without [sudo]. [cmd] --help lists them all, and [cmd] connect --help explains one.
items.cmd_connect: Connects, and waits for the result. [opt_location] chooses a location, as [cmd] locations lists them.
items.cmd_status: Shows the connection and any update on its way. [opt_watch] keeps printing it.
items.cmd_locations: Lists the server locations you can connect to.
items.cmd_service_status: Shows whether the service is running.
items.cmd_service_log: Shows the service's log. [opt_follow] follows it.
items.cmd_service_restart: Restarts the service, which disconnects the VPN. It asks for your password.
items.always_on_desc: With Always On, the VPN connects as the computer starts, before anyone signs in. While the server is out of reach it tries again, waiting longer each time. It stops when you disconnect, when another VPN app takes over, or when the server refuses the connection. Switch it on in the app's Settings, or with this command:
items.kill_switch_desc: The kill switch lets nothing out but the VPN tunnel, through an error, a crash and a reboot. With [ks_until] the block ends when you disconnect, and with [ks_lockdown] it stays after a disconnect too:
items.kill_switch_off: To lift the block, run [cmd] kill-switch off. With the service stopped, run it with [sudo].
items.updates_desc: The app updates itself: at boot and every 12 hours it looks for a newer version, downloads it, and installs it while the VPN is disconnected. Automatic Updates in the app's Settings turns this off. This command installs a newer version at once, even with updates off, and the VPN disconnects while it installs:
items.options_desc: For a script, or a machine with no desktop, add these to the install command, after its closing bracket:
items.opt_q: Asks no questions. A new install starts at boot and updates itself; an update keeps the choices you made.
items.opt_noautostart: Does not start the service at boot.
items.opt_noautoupdate: Does not update the app by itself.
items.opt_autoupdate: Updates the app by itself again, after [opt_noautoupdate].
items.opt_nodesktop: Installs the service and the commands only: no menu entry and no libraries for the window.
items.opt_desktop: Installs the menu entry and the window's libraries even where no desktop is found.

items.uninstall_desc: Right-click [app] in the application menu and choose Uninstall, or run this command:
items.uninstall_purge: It keeps your settings in /opt/[folder]/storage for a later install. Add [opt_purge] to delete them too.
items.trouble_service_fix: Run [sudo] [cmd] service start, then read [cmd] service log.
items.trouble_menu_fix: Run [cmd] ui in a terminal to see why. It is usually a library missing after an install with [opt_nodesktop].
items.trouble_standard: The window says only an administrator can use the app
items.trouble_standard_fix: Add your account to the [group_sudo] group, or to [group_wheel] where the system uses that one, then sign in again.
items.trouble_other_vpn: The app says another VPN app took over
items.trouble_other_vpn_fix: Only one app made with VpnHood! connects at a time, so connecting another one disconnects this one. It stays off, even with Always On, until you connect it again.
items.trouble_dns: Could not set the VPN's DNS servers.
items.trouble_dns_fix: Run the install command again. It sets up what the app needs for DNS.
items.trouble_nft: The kill switch needs nftables (nft), which is not installed.
items.trouble_nft_fix: Install the [pkg_nftables] package, or turn the kill switch off.
items.trouble_interface: The VPN cannot use its interface name
items.trouble_interface_fix: Another VPN has an interface called [folder], and the message says whose it is. Stop that VPN, or if it is gone and left the interface behind, run [sudo] ip link delete [folder].
